newsitem.title: UK: BBCI liquidators to pay first dividend.
newsitem.headline: BBCI liquidators to pay first dividend.

text.p: Liquidators of the collapsed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) on Friday announced that creditors would receive a first dividend payout of 24.5 cents in the dollar before the end of the year.
BCCI was shut down in 1991 with a deficit of $10 billion after evidence of widespread money laundering was uncovered.
The first dividend payment was recommended by the bank's liquidators and declared by a Luxembourg court which supervises the liquidation of two of the BCCI companies.

"We are extremeely gratified that the victims of BCCI will at last be able to recover a significant portion of their money," Ian Wight of Deloitte & Touche, which is handling liquidation in the Cayman Islands, said in a statement.
The liquidators had previously said they hoped to secure a dividend of 20 percent (or 20 cents in the dollar) but payment was dependent on Friday's court ruling in Luxembourg.
Earlier this year the liquidators concluded a $1.8 billion settlement with the former majority shareholder in BCCI, the government of Abu Dhabi.

This, in addition to efforts by US authorities which resulted in the recovery of more than $500 million from the United States, and the resolution of significant liabilities, paved the way for the first dividend payment.

"With these recoveries and the resolution of significant liabilities, the liquidators are now able to pay a first dividend that is significantly larger than anticipated," the liquidators said in a statement.

Deloitte & Touche's Wight said:"When we first began this job we feared that creditors would lose everything. The fact that creditors will now receive a quarter of their money back with further dividends to come is encouraging."
The BCCI Depositors Protection Association welcomed the dividend payout and looked forward to further payouts.
"We congratulate the depositors that at last our efforts have brought fruitful results," the association's chairman Dr Adil Ellias said in a statement.
